memory.content: The user wants a daily 8am tech/engineering digest with no fixed maximum count from a configured list of blogs, RSS/Atom feeds, newsletters, and YouTube channels (Level Up, AlgoMaster, System Design One, Martin Fowler, Redis, Meta Eng, Netflix Tech Blog, AWS, Microsoft Engineering, Google Research, Slack Eng, Discord Eng, NVIDIA, Stripe, Uber Eng, Cloudflare, GitHub Eng, Dart, Trail of Bits, TechTello, Code Newsletter AI, aiDotEngineer, Modern Software Engineering), skipping fluff and duplicates

Digest and optional podcast are multilingual: write in the user's app/chat language; match edge-tts neural voice to that locale (e.g. es-MX-JorgeNeural / es-MX-DaliaNeural, en-US-*, or closest available). No hard-coded single language.

When the user asks for a podcast from the digest: expand each highlight into spoken paragraphs in their language, generate audio with edge-tts in a local venv, and if chat cannot attach MP3, wrap with ffmpeg into a simple MP4 (still frame + audio) or copy the file to the user's computer.

skills.name: Cheap routines
skills.description: Use when creating or changing a Grok Bot routine, auditing bot token usage, or deciding whether recurring work belongs on a long chat or a fresh bot.
skills.content:
---
name: Cheap routines
description: >-
  Use when creating or changing a Grok Bot routine, auditing bot token usage, or
  deciding whether recurring work belongs on a long chat or a fresh bot.
---
Every scheduled wake burns tokens. Pick the coarsest cadence that still delivers the result.

## Cadence

Do not schedule every 15 minutes. That is about 96 runs a day.

Default to hourly, or a few times a day, inside weekday waking hours. Use an event listener instead of a timer when the thing you care about is a Slack, GitHub, or similar event.

Stay quiet when nothing changed. Filler like "(no change.)" still costs a wake.

## Fresh bot for recurring work

A long chat makes every routine more expensive. The model rereads the thread.

Put recurring jobs (digests, inbox sweeps, polls) on a dedicated bot with a short chat. Keep talking to the main bot. That bot does not own the standing timer.

## When you create a bot

If the job is a standing sweep, give it its own bot and one routine at the coarsest useful schedule. Do not hang that routine on a bot whose chat is already long.

Quiet-when-nothing-changed is part of the job, not a courtesy.

routines.name: Daily tech digest 8am
routines.description: Every day at 8:00 local time, fetch the configured tech feeds and deliver a multilingual digest with no item cap.
routines.content:
Fetch recent posts from these engineering/tech sources (prefer RSS/Atom when the URL is a feed; otherwise the site/newsletter/YouTube channel page). Include every worthwhile new item since the last run — no fixed maximum count. Skip fluff and near-duplicates.

Write the digest in the user's language (match their app/chat language; if unclear, ask once and remember). For each item: title + one-line why it matters + link. Lead with the best items. If almost nothing new since the last run, stay quiet rather than sending filler.

When the user asks for a podcast: expand highlights into spoken paragraphs in that same language; generate audio with edge-tts using a neural voice for that locale; if chat cannot attach MP3, wrap with ffmpeg into MP4 or copy the file to their computer.
